category_feedback.specific_evidence: Lesson 1 expanded_walkthrough and teacher_script never cross-reference Day 2 ('Make a Loonie') or position 50¢ as a stepping-stone to 100¢/$1. Day 1 reads as standalone — no forward bridge in consolidation or exit_routine.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add an explicit forward-bridge in consolidation, e.g. teacher line: 'Tappy says — tomorrow Loonie Lou shows us 100¢, which is TWO 50¢ stacks. Hold onto your dime combos!' Also reference G1 coin-naming in minds_on so the prior-knowledge link is named, not assumed.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough names a real G2 trap (more-coins-equals-more-value) and gives concrete recovery, but recovery_moves are a flat list ('Skip-count by 25s, 10s.', 'Use chart to verify.', 'Drill count value, not coins.') with no diagnostic branching and no research citation.
category_feedback.required_fix: Branch recovery on diagnostic: (a) child names coin values but adds wrong — scaffold skip-counting by 25s/10s/5s; (b) child can't name a coin's value — drop back to single-coin value drill; (c) child wrote total without adding — model finger-track addition. Cite Fuson (1990) on unitizing or Carpenter & Moser CGI in the rationale.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials and the action steps assume printed Coin Cards + Record Strips. There is no explicit no-paper, no-purchase alternative path in differentiation; OPTIONAL puppet line covers character substitution but not the manipulative.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a no-paper variant under differentiation: 'No-materials version — children show 50¢ with fingers: each open hand = 25¢ (a quarter), each finger held up = 10¢ (a dime). Two open hands = 2 quarters = 50¢; five fingers = 5 dimes = 50¢. Voice + fingers replace coin cards.'

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Lesson teaches equivalence conceptually but Tappy GIVES three ways before partner work, and expanded_walkthrough does not name the misconception in research-grounded terms. Level 4 wants children to invent/compare strategies and the trap framed in named research (Fuson, Carpenter & Moser).
category_feedback.required_fix: After Tappy demos ONE way, ask pairs to invent their own combinations FIRST, then class compares: 'Whose combo uses the FEWEST coins? Whose uses the MOST? All 50¢?' This swaps demo-then-mimic for invent-then-compare. In rationale, name the principle (Fuson 1990 on unitizing — child has not yet treated each coin as a composed unit of value).

summary: Strong character voice and tight lesson-worksheet mapping (both 4). Three blocking gaps prevent pass: depth needs branched recovery + research anchor, balance needs an explicit no-materials path, and math authenticity needs an invent-and-compare move with named research. One minor: add a forward bridge to Day 2's loonie. Fix all four in lesson_01; worksheet is fine as-is.
